comments.body: LGTM, are we just sunk on the ARM testing ?

@baude, I don't think we currently have a machine in CI for that (https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/28912#issuecomment-5682383070). I wouldn't advertise support for something we don't test in CI, and I'm not sure we can rely on those Packit aarch64 jobs.

> LGTM, are we just sunk on the ARM testing ?

We have it via testing-farm, but that only runs system tests and we never really ran anything other than system tests and machine tests for aarch64.

CNCF offers arm runners but we are stucked with that default ubuntu runner image there which I consider totally unsuitable since nested arm virt is not possible like we do on the x86 runners.
Now they gave us a bare metal instance but it is to large and expensive for regular PR testing IMO. I likely add it to machine-os so we can validate the image outputs there but much more than that is likely overkill.

We also test aarch64 system tests in fedora openQA but that is not upstream, so in total I am not sure we should list it as tested here since we do not gate on that even though some runs exists.
@baude If the explanation provided is enough, please merge this PR. Thanks!
